title: Explore an SVM boundary
description: Course activity for Exercise 9: choose a synthetic dataset, kernel, C, and gamma, and see how the decision boundary, support vectors, and accuracy change.
instructions: Choose a dataset (approximately linear or nonlinear), a kernel, C, and (for the polynomial/RBF kernels) gamma. The plot shows the decision regions, the training and validation points, and the support vectors -- training points close enough to the margin to shape it.
reflectionPrompts: Why can the linear kernel not separate the nonlinear dataset well?
What happens when C becomes very large?
What happens when RBF gamma becomes very large?
Which settings create a boundary that follows individual training observations too closely?
Why does perfect training accuracy not establish that the model is better?
